title-proc.eng: RE-26-03 Review and mapping of avalanche and flood hazards in Rendalen municipality

description-proc.eng: Purpose The aim of the procurement is to enter into a contract for consultancy services for reviewing and mapping landslides and flood hazards in Rendalen municipality. Rendalen municipality needs updated and documented knowledge on landslides and flood hazards as a basis for safe area management, building application processing and stand-by. The municipality lacks necessary danger zone maps for flooding in the relevant waterways and there is a need for avalanche hazard assessments in several areas. In 2026, the municipality has received a grant of financial grants from the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) to carry out investigations of safety against avalanches in steep terrain in nine areas and danger zone mapping of floods in four waterways. In order to ensure uniform and efficient execution, the assignment is announced as one combined procurement. The procurement shall provide the municipality with a basis in accordance with relevant requirements and guidelines, including NVE ́s guidelines for flood mapping and applicable requirements for safety against danger to nature. The results shall be able to be used further in planning, case handling and stand-by work. Contract 1: Review of flood and avalanche hazards Contract 2: Independent quality assurance control Contract 1 will be awarded to the tenderer ranked as number one. Contract 2 will be awarded after evaluation between the remaining tenderers who have not been awarded contract 1, in accordance with the applicable award criteria. Scope The procurement is for consultancy services for reviewing, assessing and mapping avalanche and flood hazards in Rendalen municipality. The assignment includes examining safety from avalanches in steep terrain in nine areas and danger zone mapping of floods in four waterways, as stated in the attached map and area descriptions. The delivery shall include the necessary professional surveys and analyses for the relevant areas and waterways, including review of the available data basis, site inspections, relevant calculations and modelling, as well as the preparation of reports and map products. For flood mapping, the delivery shall, among other things, provide a basis for the identification of flood-prone areas and the accompanying flood zones and flood depths. Documentation and map basis shall be submitted that the municipality can use in area planning, building application processing and stand-by. The delivery shall be clear, verifiable and adapted to further use in the municipality ́s administration. The assignment shall be carried out in accordance with the competition documents and the requirements and guidelines that apply for these types of reviews.

description-proc.eng: This is a call for market dialogue. This is not an advance notice, a procurement notice or a call for tenders, and the publication of the announcement shall not start a tendering process. The City of Helsinki is organizing a market dialogue with the aim of ensuring the feasibility of the upcoming framework agreement for artificial turf coatings through discussions with potential bidders. The current framework agreement for artificial turf surfaces for 2025–2026 will expire on 31 December 2026. The market dialogue is organized in two stages: - The market dialogue will be initiated with a joint information session on November 17, 2026, where the client will present the upcoming procurement to potential service providers and answer any questions. In addition, service providers are expected to present their own perspectives. - Following the joint information session, the contracting authority will send a questionnaire to the companies that have attended the session or registered to participate. These companies are invited to submit their responses. The information session will be held using the Teams application on November 17, 2026 at 12.00 – 13.00. (UTC +2) Registration (participants' names and email addresses) for the joint information session is requested by email to kymp.infrahankinnat@hel.fi by November 13, 2026 at 16:00 (UTC +3) at the latest. Please title the email: "Artificial turf coatings framework agreement 2025-2026, market dialogue." During the session, a general level dialogue will be conducted about the subject of the framework agreement and its definition, and an effort will be made to gather sufficient information for the procurement preparation regarding the extent of the market and the service providers' interest in participating in the procurement. The aim is to receive constructive proposals from the bidders for the final preparation of the procurement, such as the options for artificial turf coatings available on the market. The future framework agreement is related to the renovation projects of the artificial turf fields of the city of Helsinki, which will be implemented in 2027 and 2028. The estimated need for new artificial turf surfaces is 40,000–50,000 m2 per year during the contract period. The framework agreement includes the delivery of artificial turf coatings with installation in accordance with the framework contract procurement notice to be published later. The goal of the project is to clarify the selection and procurement of artificial grass coatings for future construction projects of artificial turf fields, considering: - The artificial grass coating must comply with the EU regulation on the prohibition of the use of microplastics - Diverse range of product selection for different purposes and levels of use, making it easier to choose a coating for each sport field - Clarifying and speeding up the procurement of artificial turf coatings - Cost effectiveness and future volume - To support the football clubs operating in the city of Helsinki to find new artificial turf products to replace rubber infill artificial turf. Participation in the event does not bind the participant to any possible tenders or contracts. The market dialogue does not bind the city of Helsinki to implement the procurement or to start the bidding process. The market dialogue does not bind the participating suppliers to make an offer, and on the other hand, not participating in the market dialogue has no effect in a participation to a possible tender. Suppliers are not compensated for participating in the market dialogue.

title-proc.eng: Project "PyMC"

description-proc.deu: Dieser Dienstleistungsvertrag betrifft die Python-FOSS-Bibliothek „PyMC“. Er umfasst Verbesserungen hinsichtlich der Betriebssicherheit, der Effizienz und der Geschwindigkeit der Bibliothek. Um diese Ziele zu erreichen, ist es erforderlich, eine bessere und strengere Handhabung der Benutzerkonfigurationseinstellungen zu entwerfen und zu implementieren, indem Abweichungen von den erwarteten Mustern validiert und gemeldet werden, sowie die Dokumentation zu verbessern, um Nutzer*innen und nachgelagerte Entwickler*innen über das erwartete Verhalten zu informieren. Dies umfasst auch die Entwicklung von Tests für kürzlich entwickelte Inferenz-Backends, um die Konformität dieser Implementierungen mit dem erwarteten Verhalten über alle unterstützten Backends hinweg sicherzustellen. Die Optimierung und Feinabstimmung der Leistung erfordert zudem die Entwicklung und Durchführung von Benchmarks sowie die Veröffentlichung eines reproduzierbaren Basisberichts mit Schlussfolgerungen. Die Arbeit unterstützt sowohl Personen beim Erlernen von PyMC anhand seiner Beispiel-Notebooks als auch nachgelagerte Entwickler*innen bei der Erweiterung der Log-Wahrscheinlichkeits-Infrastruktur von PyMC. Zuverlässige Konfiguration, sichtbarer Fortschritt, begrenzte Kompilierungskosten und ausführbare Beispiele helfen diesen Gruppen dabei, reproduzierbare Ergebnisse zu erzielen, ohne Fehler in der zugrunde liegenden Infrastruktur diagnostizieren zu müssen. PyMC ist eine gemeinsam genutzte statistische Infrastruktur und keine Endbenutzeranwendung. Diese Arbeit richtet sich an Forscher*innen und Praktiker*innen, die statistische Modelle erstellen, an Entwickler*innen wissenschaftlicher Software, die auf PyMC basiert, sowie an Maintainer*innen, die den Compiler, den Sampler und die Dokumentation pflegen.
description-proc.eng: This service agreement concerns the Python FOSS library "PyMC", covering improvements to the reliability of the library’s operation, efficiency and speed. Achieving these goals entails designing and implementing better, tighter, handling of user configuration settings by means of validation and reporting deviations from expected patterns, as well as improving the documentation to inform users and downstream developers of the expected behaviour. It also entails designing tests for recently developed inference backends, in order to ensure conformance of these implementations with the expected behaviour across the supported backends, in addition to optimising and tuning performance requires the designing and running of benchmarks, and publishing a reproducible baseline report with conclusions. The work supports people learning PyMC from its example notebooks and downstream developers extending its log-probability machinery. Reliable configuration, visible progress, bounded compilation costs and executable examples help these groups obtain reproducible results without having to diagnose failures inside the underlying infrastructure. PyMC is shared statistical infrastructure rather than an end-user application. This work addresses researchers and practitioners who build statistical models, developers of scientific software that depends on PyMC, and contributors who maintain its compiler, sampler and documentation.

title-proc.eng: Consultancy Services for Fund Management of three new Business Instruments

description-proc.eng: The Ministry of foreign Affairs, Green Diplomacy and Climate has entered into a contract with a Consultant (Fund Manager) to implement three business support instruments (E1, E2, and E4) as part of the Danish Government’s Strategy for Development Cooperation, “A Changing World”, appeals to Danish private companies and investors to increase their engagement and investment in the Global South, helping bridge gaps and contribute to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including climate action. The vision is that businesses which invest and expand their commercial engagements in the Global South will make significant contributions to national development agendas, including jobs, income opportunities through development of sustainable local value-chains, economic and social spin-offs from increased salaries and taxes, innovation, new technologies, and productivity-enhancements, and expansion in services. More specifically, the Strategy along with the Danish Government’s Action Plan for Effective and Economic Diplomacy seek to leverage the shared space between development cooperation and economic diplomacy, by promoting Danish companies’ investments and trade in developing partner countries. To this end, the Danish Government has initiated an initiative to strengthen business support through five business support instruments. The instruments are designed with focus on making it easier and more attractive for Danish companies to engage in emerging and developing markets, by reducing risks and clarifying and activating market potentials through partnerships, pilot projects, and business instruments providing co-investment financing and technical advice. The total amount allocated for the total initiative is DKK 850 million, of which DKK 550 million is allocated for instruments related to this tender. The five instruments focus on: E1) Early pipeline development to enlarge the pool of viable business cases; E2) Development, testing, and launching of inclusive and sustainable business models through partnerships between Danish businesses and non-commercial actors; E3) Access to finance, better enabling companies to invest and do business in high-risk Global South markets; E4) Demonstrating scalable, private sector-developed solutions with and for public authorities; and E5) Leveraging private and philanthropic capital. The five instruments are designed and should to the extent possible be managed to ensure synergies and coherence, both mutually and with the wider set of Danish private sector support engagements. The implementation of instruments E1, E2, and E4 will be managed under a Fund Management (FM) contract (Agreement) while instrument E3 and E5 will be managed by Impact Fund Denmark. This reflects a wish to concentrate the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ role on the policy and strategic management functions and to externalise the administrative and operational management functions to implementing agents. The purpose of the Agreement is to carry out the implementation and management of the three instruments, E1, E2, and E4, based on the underlying project documents and MFA Aid Management Guidelines (AMG). The Consultant will provide effective, transparent and accountable challenge fund management, covering proactive outreach and communication; call and application process implementation; contracting of selected actors/partnerships; supervision, guidance, and technical and project management backstopping of projects supported; administrative and financial management at facility level; results management and monitoring at level of each instrument; learning across the portfolio; and risk management. The objective of the Agreement is to manage and implement effectively and with accountability and transparency instruments E1, E2, and E4 and to achieve their defined objectives and results and in compliance with the MFA AMG. The Consultant’s overall tasks are: • Manage the full grant cycles of the instruments based on the project documents, including the application/call processes, with focus on efficient management, effectiveness, and accountability for funds and results. • Provide all administration of the funds including overall financial management, controls including state subsidy compliance, and verification and approval of project workplans, budgets, and reports as well as disbursements to the actors which, depending on the case, is the sole grantee, or in case of partnerships, the appointed administrative partner (commercial or non-commercial). • Provide for achievement of results as defined in the Results Framework in project documents of the instruments. • Provide outreach and communication to relevant segments of commercial actors including small/medium-size enterprises, highlight positive lessons, and ensure sharing of relevant knowledge and information that generate interest and effective participation in the instruments. • Provide relevant business and project management support and guidance to actors supported under the instruments. • Provide overall quality assurance of projects supported. • Maintain full compliance with MFA AMG and FMG, ensuring high standards of financial management, procurement, anti-corruption, and risk mitigation. • Provide relevant information and data to KLIMA on concrete projects and overall status based on request and through half annual and yearly reporting and meetings. • In relation to mid-term review or other MFA monitoring activities implement recommendations. The Agreement is divided into two phases. Phase 1 will cover the period 2027-2030 with an optional phase 2 covering up to 2035 guided by a planned mid-term review in 2029.

title-proc.eng: Procurement of consultancy services for nuclear security, including handling used fuel, radiation protection and risk assessment.

description-proc.eng: The consultant agreement shall cover the provision of technical services in support of DSA ́s core functions within regulatory work. The work shall include reviewing and assessing technical documentation and support for DSA in connection with inspections. There are three nuclear plants in Norway: the research reactor facilities in Kjeller and Halden, and the combined landfill and storage facility for low and medium radioactive waste in Himdalen. In 2018 the Norwegian government established a new government organisation, Norsk Nukleærdekommisjonering (NND), which will take over all Norwegian nuclear power plants in Kjeller, Halden and Himdalen from the original operator, Institute for Energy Engineering (IFE). NND will be responsible for the operation of the nuclear installations, the production of them and the handling of radioactive waste and used core fuel. So far the nuclear power plant in Halden has been transferred from IFE to NND, and the other two installations are close to being transferred. Before the shutdown can start, there are a number of processes that must be completed so that the operator(s) shall be able to make changes in the installations in a safe and responsible manner, and for the regulation authority (DSA) to be able to approve changes in accordance with regulations and international standards. In preparation for the liquidation and during the shutdown, there will be a need to establish a new waste handling facility, including plans for a US-developed mobile melt consolidation facility (MMC). The procurement is covered by the Security Act and reflected in the contracting authority ́s requirement specifications and security requirements. Tenderers who would like to offer in this procurement are asked separately to familiarise themselves with the stated guidelines, prerequisites and requirements.

title-proc.eng: Project "ONNX"

description-proc.deu: Dieser Dienstleistungsvertrag betrifft die offene Spezifikation „ONNX“ und die dazugehörigen Tools. Er umfasst Verbesserungen hinsichtlich der Zuverlässigkeit, Effizienz und Geschwindigkeit des Betriebs der ONNX-Kernbibliothek. ONNX ist eine herstellerneutrale, offene Spezifikation, die es ermöglicht, Modelle für maschinelles Lernen zwischen Trainings-Frameworks, Toolchains, Laufzeitumgebungen und Hardwareplattformen zu übertragen. Über die Spezifikation selbst hinaus ist ONNX auf gemeinsame Wartungsarbeiten angewiesen (Sicherheitshärtung, Release-Integrität, CI-Infrastruktur, Kompatibilität des Ökosystems und Governance), auf die sich jede Partei verlässt, die ONNX einsetzt. Die wichtigsten Ergebnisse der vertraglich vereinbarten Arbeiten werden öffentlich überprüfbare Sicherheits- und Release-Verbesserungen im Kernprojekt von ONNX sein, einschließlich des Erreichens einer Best-Practices-Zertifizierung in diesem Bereich, der gezielten Pflege von Repositories, die für das gesamte technische Ökosystem von hoher Bedeutung sind, sowie der Stärkung der Integrität der Software-Lieferkette. Die Umsetzung dieser Ergebnisse erfordert eine Überprüfung der bestehenden Codebasis der Tools und der CI/CD-Konfigurationen, die Entwicklung von Praktiken zur Mitwirkung sowie die Identifizierung etwaiger Mängel anhand der Zertifizierungsanforderungen und -prüfungen, bevor Lösungen erarbeitet und umgesetzt werden, um die genannten Aspekte mit den Zertifizierungsvorgaben in Einklang zu bringen. Hinzu kommen Governance-Maßnahmen, die erforderlich sind, um diese Ergebnisse dauerhaft zu sichern und die künftige Weiterentwicklung von ONNX auf der Grundlage einer Analyse der Herausforderungen und Chancen zu fördern.
description-proc.eng: This service agreement concerns the open specification "ONNX" and its associated tools, covering improvements to the reliability of the library’s operation, efficiency and speed. ONNX is a vendor-neutral, open specification allowing machine-learning models to be moved between training frameworks, toolchains, runtimes, and hardware platforms. Beyond the specification itself, ONNX depends on shared maintenance work (security hardening, release integrity, CI infrastructure, ecosystem compatibility, and governance) that every vendor using ONNX relies on. The primary outcomes of the contracted work will be publicly verifiable security and release improvements in the core ONNX project, including obtaining certification for best practices in the field; targeted maintenance of high-impact ecosystem repositories; strengthening the supply-chain integrity. Realising these outcomes entails reviewing the current codebase of tools, CI/CD setups, and contribution practices, and identifying any shortcomings as per the certification requirements and checks, before researching and implementing solutions to bring the above aspects to compliance, in addition to the governance work required to sustain those results and to foster future development of ONNX, based on an analysis of the challenges and opportunities.
